skill.name: ai-code-cleanup
skill.description: Clean up AI-assisted code by removing redundant comments, defensive bloat, unnecessary type workarounds, and style drift while preserving behavior.
skill.summary: Remove AI-generated artifacts from code before review or merge.
skill.author: Joseph OBrien

security_audit.summary: Static hits are false positives from Markdown code fences, inline code, regex dots, and example snippets. No prompt injection, malware intent, or data exfiltration evidence was found. One semantic risk remains: the cleanup guidance can encourage removal of validation or error handling without proof that it is redundant.

remediation.issue: Validation and error handling can be removed too broadly.
remediation.suggestion: Require proof that callers or framework boundaries already validate data before removing guards, catches, or input checks.

remediation.issue: Examples show removing userId validation without showing the trusted boundary.
remediation.suggestion: Add context that the input is already validated, or change the example to keep boundary validation for user-controlled data.

remediation.issue: Cleanup criteria rely on judgment and may be applied mechanically.
remediation.suggestion: Add a checklist that preserves authorization, authentication, validation, and security logging unless tests and design contracts prove redundancy.

semantic_findings.title: Overbroad Defensive Code Removal Guidance
semantic_findings.description: The skill tells agents to remove redundant validation and shows an example that removes userId validation and catch handling. Without proving validation exists upstream, this can delete security controls.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The guidance and example explicitly remove validation and error handling, but later best practices say to keep legitimate controls. The risk is contextual rather than clearly malicious.

content.value_statement: AI-assisted code can include redundant comments, defensive bloat, and style drift. This skill guides targeted cleanup while preserving behavior and tests.
actual_capabilities: Identifies obvious comments, redundant explanations, and documentation that does not match nearby style.
Flags unnecessary try/catch blocks, null checks, and validation when existing contracts make them redundant.
Finds type casts, any usage, and TypeScript suppression comments used as workarounds.
Compares changed files against project style and recommends surgical edits.
Uses branch diffs to focus cleanup on modified files.
Provides a refactoring plan template for larger cleanup work.
limitations: Cannot prove behavior is unchanged without running project tests.
Requires human judgment before removing validation or error handling.
Works best with enough surrounding code to infer project conventions.
Does not include an executable cleanup script or automated linter.

use_cases.title: Prepare an AI-built pull request
use_cases.description: Remove redundant comments, noisy guards, and style drift before a reviewer sees the branch.

use_cases.title: Standardize mixed AI edits
use_cases.description: Bring AI-assisted changes back in line with local naming, formatting, and error-handling conventions.

use_cases.title: Plan a larger cleanup
use_cases.description: Document code smells, target state, testing steps, and rollback plans before refactoring a component.

prompt_templates.title: Clean My Branch
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the current branch for AI-generated cleanup issues. List redundant comments, defensive bloat, type workarounds, and style inconsistencies before editing.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare A Pull Request
prompt_templates.prompt: Clean the files changed in this pull request. Preserve behavior, keep legitimate validation, and run the project checks that apply.

prompt_templates.title: Target A Risky Module
prompt_templates.prompt: Review src/api for AI-generated artifacts. Explain each proposed removal, identify any validation that must stay, and make small grouped edits.

prompt_templates.title: Create A Refactoring Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the refactoring plan template for the selected component. Include current smells, target state, step order, risk controls, tests, and rollback steps.

output_examples.input: Clean redundant comments in an authentication helper.
output: Removed comments that repeated simple assignments and return statements.
Kept one comment that explained a non-obvious security decision.
Reported that behavior should be verified with the existing authentication tests.

output_examples.input: Review a branch after an AI coding session.
output: Found noisy null checks in files where callers already validate inputs.
Kept boundary validation for user-controlled request data.
Recommended running type checks and the affected unit test suite.

output_examples.input: Plan cleanup for a service module.
output: Created a phased cleanup plan with current smells and target outcomes.
Listed test coverage needed before removing defensive code.
Included a rollback plan for each cleanup phase.

best_practices: Review the diff first and limit edits to changed files unless the user expands scope.
Keep validation, authorization checks, and error handling unless redundancy is proven.
Run tests or type checks after each meaningful cleanup batch.
anti_patterns: Removing guards because they look verbose without proving callers validate the data.
Changing architecture while doing a cleanup pass.
Replacing clear code with clever shortcuts only to reduce line count.

faq.question: What does this skill clean up?
faq.answer: It targets redundant comments, defensive bloat, type workarounds, style drift, and other common AI-generated artifacts.

faq.question: Can it change code behavior?
faq.answer: It is designed to preserve behavior, but users should verify changes with tests and review.

faq.question: Should it remove validation code?
faq.answer: Only remove validation when another trusted layer already enforces the same rule. Keep checks for untrusted input.

faq.question: Does it run automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples for an AI assistant to apply during a cleanup task.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: The skill metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: When should I use the refactoring template?
faq.answer: Use it when cleanup is broad enough to need phases, risk tracking, tests, or rollback planning.
